```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(knbsdata)
```

This page states plainly what this release can and cannot do, and why. It is
worth reading before relying on the package for anything that matters.

## Registered sources

```{r}
knbs_sources()
```

```{r}
knbs_status()
```

`knbs_status(live = TRUE)` contacts the verified sources. It never contacts a
source at stability `discovery`, because those have placeholder endpoints and
there is nothing to call.

## What each stability level means

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `discovery` | The endpoint has not been verified. Unusable, and never contacted. |
| `experimental` | Verified and tested, but not documented by its publisher, so it could change without notice. |
| `beta` | Verified, documented and monitored over time. |
| `stable` | A schema contract the package expects to keep. |
| `deprecated` | Scheduled for removal. |

Nothing in this release is above `experimental`.

## What works

**The survey catalogue**, via the Kenya National Data Archive:
`knbs_search_surveys()`, `knbs_survey_metadata()`, `knbs_variables()` and
`knbs_survey_files()`. The archive exposes a JSON API that needs no credentials
for metadata. 129 studies covering 1969–2022 were catalogued at the time of the
audit.

**Open survey microdata**, via the FinAccess portal
(`finaccess.knbs.or.ke`): `knbs_finaccess_files()`,
`knbs_download_finaccess()` and `knbs_read_microdata()`. The Central Bank of
Kenya, KNBS and FSD Kenya publish the anonymised, weighted microdata of the
FinAccess household surveys — 2006, 2009, 2013, 2016, 2021 and 2024 — and of
two MSE Tracker Survey waves for anyone to download, with questionnaires,
manuals and reports. The portal is a web page linking Google Drive files, so
the package keeps its own catalogue of them, and holds every download to it:
served name and size before the transfer, size and SHA-256 after. Three
properties to keep in mind:

- **The portal states no licence.** FSD Kenya's terms for the 2013 survey
  restrict the data to research and forbid redistribution without written
  agreement; assume nothing wider. The terms travel in each file's sidecar
  and metadata, and no file is bundled with the package.
- **Some portal labels are wrong**, and the catalogue records what each link
  actually serves: the MSE Tracker Wave II formats are swapped, and the 2006
  and 2009 "Questionnaire" archives hold the survey data too.
- **The 2013 survey's Stata copy sits behind a registration form** on
  Harvard Dataverse. It is listed, never fetched; its SPSS copy is open.

**Publications**, via the KNBS website's media library:
`knbs_publications()` and `knbs_download_publication()`. The site's WordPress
REST API lists roughly 1,600 documents — statistical releases, survey reports,
Economic Survey chapters and workbooks — with direct, ungated file URLs.
Downloads are verified, checksummed and given a provenance sidecar.

Two properties of this source to keep in mind:

- `release_date` is the date a file reached the website, not the publication's
  reference period. The `year` column is read from the title, and is `NA` when
  the title names none.
- The media library also holds speeches, launch remarks and forms. What counts
  as a publication is your `query`, not a curated list.

**Census tables**, via the KNBS census data service (`data.knbs.or.ke`):
`knbs_indicators()` and `knbs_get_indicator()`. Thirty-two tables from the
2019 Population and Housing Census as JSON-stat, under an explicit CC BY 4.0
statement, with geography down to sub-county and leading zeros intact. See
`vignette("census-indicators")`.

One property of this source to keep in mind: **its API host is HTTP-only** —
no TLS listener exists — so traffic to it is unencrypted in transit. It
carries public census aggregates and no credentials, and the registry records
the exception explicitly rather than hiding it.

**The economy**, via the KNBS Data Portal (`opendata.knbs.or.ke`): 323 SDMX
dataflows across five statistical domains — GDP by activity and expenditure,
GFCF, GNI, production accounts, CPI by division and region, balance of
payments, trade, money and banking, county government finance, employment,
agriculture, tourism, health and justice. `knbs_indicators()` lists them
(`source_id` `"knbs_opendata"`) and `knbs_get_indicator()` fetches one by its
SDMX id, for example `"DF_NAT_GDPCP"`. Three properties to keep in mind: the
portal states **no licence**; its geography codes are **SDMX area codes, not
census territories** (never join them against `knbs_geographies()`); and
single-category dimensions fold into `knbs_metadata()` notes rather than
arriving as constant columns.

**Consumer prices**, via the KNBS CPI Explorer (`cpiexplorer.knbs.or.ke`):
`knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS")`, `"CPI_INFLATION_YOY"` and
`"CPI_INFLATION_MOM"` — monthly from January 2009, nationally and by the CPI
collection strata (the Nairobi income bands, Nairobi Combined, Rest of
Urban) — plus `knbs_retail_prices()`, the monthly national average retail
prices of the 22 CPI basket commodities. See
`vignette("census-indicators")`.

Three properties of this source to keep in mind, all carried in
`knbs_metadata()` on every result:

- **The portal states no licence**, unlike the census service's CC BY 4.0
  footer, and does not state the index base period.
- **Its regions are collection strata, not census territories.** Their codes
  must never be joined against `knbs_geographies()`.
- **Six listed regions — the former provinces — carry no data in any
  period.** Asking for them returns zero rows, because that is the source's
  answer.

**Gross County Product and the republished datasets**, via Kenya Open Data
for Africa (`kenya.opendataforafrica.org`): 202 datasets — 169 sourced from
KNBS, the rest from the Central Bank of Kenya, ministries and agencies —
including the one thing no first-party portal serves as data: Gross County
Product (`knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc")` — GVA shares plus constant- and
current-price GCP for all 47 counties, 2013–2020). `knbs_indicators()` lists
them (`source_id` `"opendataforafrica"`).

This source is different in kind from the others, and its honesty caveats
are correspondingly heavier:

- **It is a republisher, not the publisher.** The portal is operated on the
  Knoema data platform and is listed on KNBS's own portals page; every
  result's `knbs_metadata()` names the portal and points at the original
  producer. Where a first-party portal serves the same data, prefer the
  first-party portal.
- **Its vintage can lag the PDFs.** The GCP dataset is the 2021 edition;
  KNBS has since published newer GCP years as PDF reports only. The
  metadata carries the portal's own publication and update dates so the lag
  is visible, not hidden.
- **Licence labels vary by dataset** and are carried verbatim — most
  KNBS-sourced datasets say "Public Domain"; datasets without a label say
  "Not stated by the source".
- **Its geography codes are the portal's own region codes** (`KE`,
  `KE-700-BA`, …), not census territories; never join them against
  `knbs_geographies()`.
- **A dataset may mix frequencies** — annual, quarterly and monthly series
  side by side under one id. Annual periods are integer years and
  sub-annual ones are Dates, which cannot share a column, so a mixed
  dataset asks you to choose (`frequency = "annual"`) rather than picking
  one silently.
- **Its edge sometimes challenges automated clients.** The package
  identifies itself transparently and speaks plain HTTP/1.1, which the
  portal serves; if a challenge page comes back anyway, that is an access
  gate and you get `knbs_error_access_restricted` — the package never
  solves or retries a challenge. Trying again later usually suffices.

**Health and demography**, via the DHS Program's Indicator Data API
(`api.dhsprogram.com`): the indicators of the Kenya Demographic and Health
Surveys (1989–2022), which KNBS implements, and of the 2015 and 2020 Malaria
Indicator Surveys — 4,115 of them, listed by `knbs_indicators()` with
`source_id` `"dhs_program"` and fetched by id, for example
`knbs_get_indicator("CN_NUTS_C_HA2")` (children stunted). Each comes for
every survey that measured it, by background characteristic, by the former
provinces, and from 2014 by county. KNBS's own KDHS portal is a dashboard
with no data API, and answered with an error when checked. Properties to
keep in mind:

- **County rows carry census codes**; province and malaria-zone rows carry
  none, since no census code exists for them.
- **Several values can describe one group.** Where the DHS Program reports
  more than one reference period, every value is kept and `preferred`
  marks the one it prefers.
- **A few ids are reused.** The API lists 27 indicator ids twice; where one
  serves two different values for the same survey and group, the package
  refuses it with `knbs_error_validation_failed` rather than choose.
- **The terms ask for a citation**, which `knbs_cite()` gives in the form
  the API specifies. No licence is stated.
- **Its robots file bars `/rest/dhs/`**, the API itself, to every client,
  while its documentation invites applications to use it. The package reads
  the rule as addressed to crawlers: it asks only for what you request, one
  indicator at a time, under its own name, throttled and cached, and never
  walks the API.

**Statistical Abstract tables**, via the KNBS website's chapter workbooks:
`knbs_abstract_tables()` and `knbs_abstract_table()`. 48 tables of the 2025
edition, across 13 chapters — the whole National Accounts chapter and 33
tables from twelve more — extract into tidy observations by hand-verified
recipes. Extraction is deliberately strict: layout anchors, section labels
and pinned reference values are re-checked on every read, and a workbook
that has drifted is refused with a classed error rather than
re-interpreted. Tables not yet curated remain verified *downloads*
(`knbs_download_publication()`). See `vignette("statistical-abstract")`.

## What does not, and why

### The archive's microdata cannot be downloaded

The archive requires an account for every download. `knbs_download_microdata()`
explains the official access process and stops. The package does not automate
sign-in, licence acceptance or approval workflows. Microdata are downloaded
only where the producers publish them for anyone, as the FinAccess surveys
are.

This is worth understanding rather than working around: `access_type` of
`public_use` describes the archive's *terms* — public-use files exist — not
whether a program may fetch them.

### Documentation files are not listed

Questionnaires, reports and technical documents have no machine-readable
listing at the archive. Reaching them would mean parsing a web page, which this
package does not do. The `catalogue_url` column from `knbs_search_surveys()`
opens the study on the archive's own site, where they are linked.

### The newest Gross County Product years are still documents

GCP is data now — but only the 2021 edition (2013–2020), through the Open
Data for Africa republisher above; no first-party KNBS portal serves it as
data (checked exhaustively). The editions published since extend the series
past 2020 as PDF reports only, reachable through
`knbs_publications("gross county product")`. If the newest county figures
matter, read the PDF; the metadata on the data version dates its vintage
precisely so the gap is never invisible.

### Geography: one vintage, no boundaries, no classifications

`knbs_geographies()` serves the 2019 census frame — Kenya, 47 counties,
sub-counties, with names and parent codes, read from the census service's own
Territory dimension. What it does not serve, because nothing has been
verified: other vintages, crosswalks between coding systems, boundary
geometries (`knbs_boundaries()` does not exist) and statistical
classifications.

### Variable documentation is uneven

Some studies are catalogued with no variable metadata at all, including the most
recent one at the time of the audit. `knbs_variables()` returns zero rows for
those. That is the archive's answer, not a failure.

## How you will know if something changes

The package checks the *shape* of every response, not just its status code.
The archive answers unknown paths with `200` and a study record rather than a
404, so a renamed endpoint would otherwise deliver the wrong object convincingly.
When a payload lacks the fields its operation requires, you get
`knbs_error_schema_changed` and a note that the endpoint has probably moved.

A scheduled job runs `knbs_status(live = TRUE)` weekly against the verified
sources.

## Reporting a change

If a source has moved, changed shape or changed its access rules, please open a
[data source change issue](https://github.com/Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata/issues/new/choose).
Public URLs only — never session-bound URLs, tokens or cookies.

## Disclaimer

`knbsdata` is an independent open-source project. It is not an official KNBS
product unless and until KNBS formally adopts or endorses it. Consult the
original KNBS source for authoritative definitions, revisions, access conditions
and official releases.
